texts.preamble: Ntex Transportation Services Pvt. Ltd. ... vs The State Of Telangana on 17 October, 2025 Author: Juvvadi Sridevi Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Criminal Revision Case No.753 of 2025 Order :
texts.facts: In furtherance of its business operations, petitioner's company has taken a warehouse building on lease situated at Devarayamjal village. In the course of its business the petitioner company has stored the properties in its warehouse for the purpose of distribution to retailers on their demand. JS, J 4.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner company is incorporated under the provision of company's Act 2013 and engaged in the business of transportation, distribution and other logistic solutions operating under the name and style of "Elastic Run". Learned counsel further submits that the petitioner has stored a list of 18 items, out of which 14 and 15 were particularly kept aside from the remaining goods and was kept separately in the said warehouse in a separate place, earmarked for returning to its vendors as the same had expired. While the matter stood thus, Police, Pet Basheerabad, on 01.07.2025 raided the warehouse of the petitioner alleging that the petitioner company is selling expired goods and without considering the explanation offered by the petitioner the police have seized the goods in the warehouse alleging that the goods do not have expiry dates and as such have expired and filed an FIR vide No.1069 of 2025. Subsequently a petition under section 451 of Cr.P.C. was filed by the petitioner for return of goods before the trial Court, but the learned Magistrate dismissed the same vide impugned order. 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the goods which were seized from the warehouse are perishable in nature and there is every chance of decay. Further the fact that when the goods were seized from the warehouse of the petitioner, there would be an inventory of the same and by returning the property to the petitioner, there would be no hindrance to the investigation in Ntex Transportation Services Pvt. Ltd. ... vs The State Of Telangana on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74684194/ 1 any manner. It is JS, J further submitted that if the seized goods, if not handed over to the petitioner, the items will perish and will not be of any value/use to the petitioner herein, causing irreparable damage to the petitioner. 6. He further submitted that in view of mention of expiry dates on the goods there are some exemptions from certain labeling requirements as per Food Safety and Standards (Labellilng and Display) Regulations, 2020 which reads as under: 8. Exemptions from certain labeling requirements- (1) Where the surface area of the package is not more than 100 square centimeters, the label of such package shall be exempted from the requirements of list of ingredients, Lot number or batch number or code number, nutritional information, labeling of irradiated food, declaration of food additives, license number and logo the name and complete address of the importer and instructions for use, but these information shall be given on the multi-unit packages. 2[(1) (a) The 'date of manufacture' and Use by date or expiry date' may not be required to be mentioned on the package having surface area of less than thirty square centimeters but this information shall be given on the multi-unit packages] Therefore, in the case of small units, each and every unit will not be given details of manufacturing and expiry dates. 7. He submits that among the seized stock, there are stocks of edible products such as candies and toffees for sale in view of the ensuing festival i.e. Diwali. Hence, he prayed to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the JS, J impugned order passed by the trial Court and to direct the trial Court for release of the goods. 8. On the other hand, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor fairly admits that the petition may be allowed subject to preparation of inventory of the goods after duly recording the evidence by the trial Court in accordance with the provisions under section 497 of BNSS. 9. Section 497 of BNSS reads as follows: (1) When any property is produced before any Criminal Court or the Magistrate empowered to take cognizance or commit the case for trial during any investigation, inquiry or trial, the Court or the Magistrate may make such order as it thinks fit for the proper custody of such property pending the conclusion of the investigation, inquiry or trial, and, if the property is subject to speedy and natural decay, or if it is otherwise expedient so to do, the Court or the Magistrate may, after recording such evidence as it thinks necessary, order it to be sold or otherwise disposed of. Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "property" includes-- Ntex Transportation Services Pvt. Ltd. ... vs The State Of Telangana on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74684194/ 2 (a) property of any kind or document which is produced before the Court or which is in its custody; (b) any property regarding which an offence appears to have been committed or which appears to have been used for the commission of any offence. (2) The Court or the Magistrate shall, within a period of fourteen days from the production of the property referred to in sub- section (1) before it, prepare a statement of such property containing its description in such form and manner as the State Government may, by rules, provide. JS, J (3) The Court or the Magistrate shall cause to be taken the photograph and if necessary, videograph on mobile phone or any electronic media, of the property referred to in sub-section (1). (4) The statement prepared under sub-section (2) and the photograph or the videography taken under sub-section (3) shall be used as evidence in any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under the Sanhita. (5) The Court or the Magistrate shall, within a period of thirty days after the statement has been prepared under sub-section (2) and the photograph or the videography has been taken under sub-section (3), order the disposal, destruction, confiscation or delivery of the property in the manner specified hereinafter. 10.
